target_customer: Indian retail users who bet on event outcomes, and brokers or gaming apps that integrate its exchange by API
problem: People wanted to trade on opinions about news and events, with no regulated Indian venue. TradeX runs a prediction market exchange and offers broker APIs.
business_model: Exchange fee on real money event trading plus B2B API
product_category: Prediction market and opinion trading app

founders.name: Divij Goyal
founders.background_notes: YC page: former S&P 500 trader and product lead; YourStory says the app started in January 2021.

founders.name: Indrajeet Roy
founders.background_notes: From the YC page; Dealroom also lists him as co-founder.

competitors.name: Probo
competitors.what: Indian opinion trading app on real world events
competitors.funding_then: Seed reportedly about 2.5M from Sequoia and Elevation in March 2021 per one profile, and a Series A planned in 2022; unverified

technical_complexity.rationale: A matching exchange and payments for real money events needs reliable engineering and risk controls, but is standard fintech software.

defensibility.rationale: Liquidity could help, but rivals like Probo copied the model and the legal status was uncertain.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquirer; real money operations stopped after state bans and SEBI scrutiny.

market_need_then: Indian users already engaged with real money gaming and trading apps and early opinion trading apps raised venture money in 2021 to 2022.

identity.voice_and_tone: Pitched as a calculated bet on news

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by YourStory and Entrackr; a different TradeX Markets crypto product and a virtual F and O trading app share the name.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name shared with unrelated products, limited brand press beyond launch coverage.

pivots.to: Free to play social prediction model
pivots.why: Legal restrictions and regulatory challenges in India, per Storyboard18 as summarized by search

outcome_analysis: TradeX raised 1 million dollars in early 2022 for an Indian prediction market and never raised a verified later round. Real money trading was shut down in 2025 after state bans and SEBI scrutiny, and it moved toward a free to play model. The legal status of the product, not demand, was the binding limit.
notes: Total raised is reported inconsistently: 4.5M (Crowdfund Insider, Persana), 1.5M (CB Insights), 1.13M (TheCompanyCheck); unverified. Status stays Active on the directory while real money operations ended in 2025, so exit is none. Education of Goyal and Shrivastava not on the YC page. The Probo competitor source is undated; dated close to the batch by a February 2022 report of its Series A plan. The Probo funding figure comes from one profile and is unverified.
